items.title: Formulas over a structure translate to formulas over its labelled tree at the same quantifier complexity, and back
items.author: David Gonzalez; Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 234-249: for every structure A and every infinitary formula over its vocabulary there is a formula of the same quantifier rank over the labelled tree of A that holds at every node above a tuple exactly when the original holds at that tuple, and conversely every formula over the tree has an equivalent formula over A of the same rank. The statement contains no construction, and the proof (source lines 250-286) has to build both directions: the push-forward direction by disjunctive normal form for the quantifier-free case, then an induction whose existential step replaces a quantifier by a quantifier over successor nodes, with the height and label conditions read off the tree; the pull-back direction is a different kind of argument, constructing a parameterised Turing computable embedding by choosing, for a fixed tuple of nodes, the lexicographically least finite tuples whose subtrees are isomorphic to the ones described by that tuple, and then invoking the pull-back theorem along it. Neither the disjunctive normal form reduction nor the embedding construction is visible in the statement.
